title: Carmela Squash (Carmela F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Carmela squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety from Allied Botanical (Condor). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Carmela squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety, also sold or known as Carmela F1 or Carmela calabaza. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Carmela squash is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Carmela F1 or Carmela calabaza, this is the same squash. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [squash variety finder](/crop-varieties/squash), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: harvest 80 to 90 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit squash fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** Harvest 80 to 90 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Dark green skin, yellow orange flesh, 4 to 5 kg.
Intermediate resistance to squash leaf curl virus.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: in Allied Botanical's calabaza lineup, only evidence is the company's own listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual squash on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Carmela squash

Choose a fruit size your buyer wants, from small round ones for households to big flat ones for the market. A thick, deep orange flesh keeps longer and sells better. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Carmela F1 the same as Carmela?
items.a: Yes. Carmela F1 is another name for Carmela. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Carmela?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
